profile.title: Pattern Manual for Service Systems Thinking
profile.canonical_definition: David Ing’s 2016 proposal to translate lessons from generative pattern languages into service systems thinking, reframing patterns around voices on issues, affording values and spatio-temporal frames.
profile.summary: A proposal for carrying generative pattern-language learning into service systems.
profile.why_it_matters: It shows how a method can be translated between domains only by changing its ontology and pattern form.
common_misreadings: It does not claim the built-environment pattern form can simply be reused unchanged.
profile.editorial_note: Public account based on named sources; documentary provenance, interpretation and evaluative claims are kept distinct.

connections.scope_conditions: Limited to the named sources. Documentary connection, conceptual influence, teaching use and effectiveness are distinct claims.

connections.source_locator: Pattern Manual paper, pp. 12-14, comparison of Alexandrian form with voices on issues, affording values and spatio-temporal frames
connections.scope_conditions: The paper advances a proposal for discussion and explicitly frames it as an adaptation and extension, not a settled standard.
connections.inference_method: close reading of the author paper and publication record
connections.notes: The proposed format changes the unit of a pattern from context-problem-solution to voices/issues, affording values and spatio-temporal frames for service systems.

connections.source_locator: Pattern Manual paper, p. 13, paragraph beginning 'Extending issues to explicitly identify voices'
connections.scope_conditions: The paper operationalises perspectives as named voices around an issue; it does not guarantee that every affected perspective will be represented.
connections.inference_method: close reading of the author paper
connections.notes: Ing makes voices explicit in the service-systems pattern form so collective and individual perspectives are represented before action decisions.
